record.original_question: Define the degrees of freedom of a Costas array of order n as the smallest k <= n for which there exist indices i1 < i2 < ... < ik in [n] such that, for any prescribed values f1, ..., fk in [n], there is at most one Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] with f(ij)=fj for all j. Determine this quantity for Costas arrays of order n, and if possible improve the definition so it captures the phenomenon more effectively.

evidence.quote: More precisely, this concept is now defined [23] as the smallest k ≤ n such that there exist i1 < i2 < . . . < ik ∈ [n] with the property that, for any arbitrary collection of values f1, . . . , fk ∈ [n], the set of functions {f : [n] → [n] : f(ij) = fj , j ∈ [k]} contains at most one Costas permutation.
Problem 3. Determine the “degrees of freedom” of Costas arrays of order n, as defined in the second approach above. If possible, improve on this definition.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A Costas permutation of order $n$ is a bijection $f:[n]\to[n]$ (where $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$) such that all vectors $(j-i,\,f(j)-f(i))$ with $1\le i<j\le n$ are distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer $h$ the function $i\mapsto f(i+h)-f(i)$ is injective on its domain. Define the degrees of freedom of Costas permutations of order $n$ to be the smallest integer $k\le n$ for which there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k$ in $[n]$ with the following property: for every prescribed tuple of values $(f_1,\dots,f_k)\in[n]^k$, the set $\{f:[n]\to[n]\,:\,f(i_j)=f_j\text{ for }j=1,\dots,k\}$ contains at most one Costas permutation. Determine this quantity as a function of $n$, and, if possible, propose an improved definition that better captures the phenomenon of how few coordinates suffice to determine a Costas permutation.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the degrees of freedom of Costas arrays of order n is listed as an open problem. Partial results exist: studies have shown the number of degrees of freedom is surprisingly small and have proved partial results for Golomb and Welch Costas permutations, but no closed-form determination for general n is known.

status_evidence.title: Some results on the degrees of freedom of Costas arrays
status_evidence.snippet: Studies degrees of freedom of Costas permutations, finding the number is surprisingly small with partial results for Golomb and Welch Costas permutations.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known for the degrees of freedom of Costas arrays.

status_evidence.title: On the degrees of freedom of Costas permutations and other constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates degrees of freedom of Costas permutations, providing partial bounds and exploring the concept further.
status_evidence.claim: The general determination remains open; only partial bounds are obtained.
